ch2_town_arrival.speaker: patch
ch2_town_arrival.text: Lanternfold Harbor! Festival town! Lights, music, adoring crowds. I can feel the adoration from here.

ch2_town_arrival.speaker: patch
ch2_town_arrival.text: ...It's a bit damp. The lanterns are all out. And the bunting's sort of... dripping.

ch2_town_arrival.speaker: patch
ch2_town_arrival.text: Fine. We find whoever's in charge, fix the festival, and they name a lantern after me. Big one. Orange.

lamplighters_intro.speaker: lamplighters
lamplighters_intro.text: A visitor! Hello! We're the Lamplighter Sisters. We were cut from the same strip of paper, so we share everything. Including sentences.

lamplighters_intro.speaker: lamplighters
lamplighters_intro.text: The festival's meant to be tonight. Every year since the book was made. But the damp got into the wicks and every lantern in town went out.

lamplighters_intro.speaker: patch
lamplighters_intro.text: And you can't relight them yourselves because...?

lamplighters_intro.speaker: lamplighters
lamplighters_intro.text: We're holding hands. Permanently. It makes ladders very complicated.

lamplighters_intro.speaker: lamplighters
lamplighters_intro.text: There are five festival lanterns around town. Light them and we'll pay you in Scraps and undying gratitude. Mostly Scraps.

lamplighters_progress.speaker: lamplighters
lamplighters_progress.text: Still some dark corners out there. Five lanterns in all. Check by the hedges, the houses, and down near the water.

lamplighters_done.speaker: lamplighters
lamplighters_done.text: Look at it! The whole harbor's glowing. It's not as bright as it used to be. The paper's gone a bit wavy.

lamplighters_done.speaker: lamplighters
lamplighters_done.text: But it's ours, and it's lit. That counts for more than we thought it would. Here, take these Scraps.

lamplighters_done.speaker: patch
lamplighters_done.text: And the lantern you're naming after me?

lamplighters_repeat.speaker: lamplighters
lamplighters_repeat.text: If you've got rhythm, the shadow theater's running a show tonight. The crowd's tough. They're made of cardboard.

corrugate_intro.speaker: corrugate
corrugate_intro.text: Well. A fox. Haven't seen a fox on this page since the book was new. You're missing a bit.

corrugate_intro.speaker: patch
corrugate_intro.text: Lost it in a duel with a sea serpent. You should see the serpent.

corrugate_intro.speaker: corrugate
corrugate_intro.text: Hm. I'm Corrugate. Captain, retired. That's my boat. It leaks. And under the harbor flap there's something big and inky that's been pulling the whole town down, one plank at a time.

corrugate_intro.speaker: patch
corrugate_intro.text: So let's go and punch it.

corrugate_intro.speaker: corrugate
corrugate_intro.text: The flap's soaked shut and my boat's got a hole you could post a letter through. I'd need real tape. Not drawn tape. Real.

corrugate_intro.speaker: corrugate
corrugate_intro.text: On the Great Light's table, yes. Through that page corner by the dock. Mind yourself. Everything out there is the size of a house, and none of it is on your side.

corrugate_need_tape.speaker: corrugate
corrugate_need_tape.text: The page corner by the dock goes out onto the table. The tape roll's out there somewhere. Peel off a strip. Don't let it peel you.

corrugate_cat.speaker: corrugate
corrugate_cat.text: Real tape! On your tail, no less. Suits you. Very modern.

corrugate_cat.speaker: patch
corrugate_cat.text: It's a Tape Tail. I can throw it. It sticks to brass rings and pulls me along. I'm basically a superhero now.

corrugate_cat.speaker: corrugate
corrugate_cat.text: Good, because I've a superhero problem. Crumple, my ship's cat, has gone and sat on the mooring post out across the water. Won't come in. Sulks when it's wet.

corrugate_cat.speaker: corrugate
corrugate_cat.text: I'm not going out there. I'm a sea captain who is afraid of the sea now, and I'd rather we didn't talk about it.

corrugate_cat.speaker: patch
corrugate_cat.text: You stand on that dock, Captain. I'll swing across on the brass rings.

corrugate_cat_progress.speaker: corrugate
corrugate_cat_progress.text: She's out on the little mooring post across the water. Throw your tape at the brass ring by the dock's end and you'll see.

corrugate_joins.speaker: corrugate
corrugate_joins.text: There she is. Dry as a biscuit and furious about it. Thank you, fox.

corrugate_joins.speaker: corrugate
corrugate_joins.text: Right. I patched the boat with the rest of your tape. Which means I've run out of excuses.

corrugate_joins.speaker: corrugate
corrugate_joins.text: The harbor flap. I'll lift it. But I'm coming with you, slowly, and if anything wet touches me I reserve the right to complain.

heist_arrival.speaker: patch
heist_arrival.text: Gran's table. At night. Okay. Very big, very dark, very quiet. Totally fine.

heist_arrival.speaker: patch
heist_arrival.text: Right. Grab the tape, get back to the book, nobody gets flattened by a mug. Easy.

flap_arrival.speaker: corrugate
flap_arrival.text: Under the harbor. Haven't been down here since the book was dry. It used to be blue, you know. Properly blue.

flap_arrival.speaker: patch
flap_arrival.text: Now it's ink. Lots of ink. Is it supposed to drip?

flap_arrival.speaker: corrugate
flap_arrival.text: No. Watch the gaps. Fall in that and you'll come out a different colour, if you come out.

kraken_arrival.speaker: patch
kraken_arrival.text: That's not a sea. That's a spill. With an eye.

kraken_arrival.speaker: corrugate
kraken_arrival.text: Blotch. I'd know it anywhere. It's been eating the harbor from underneath.

kraken_arrival.speaker: corrugate
kraken_arrival.text: Blotting paper soaks up ink. Drop it on the beast and it'll go limp. Then you swipe it, fox. I'll be here. Shouting encouragement. From the dry bit.

kraken_drizzle.speaker: kraken
kraken_drizzle.text: ...I just wanted... it to stop... raining...

kraken_drizzle.speaker: patch
kraken_drizzle.text: It talked. Why does it talk?

kraken_drizzle.speaker: corrugate
kraken_drizzle.text: Look at the ink, fox. That's not harbor ink. That's Weather Page ink. That's Drizzle's ink.

kraken_drizzle.speaker: patch
kraken_drizzle.text: Drizzle? The little rain cloud? The one that waters the meadow and says good morning to everyone?

kraken_drizzle.speaker: corrugate
kraken_drizzle.text: The flood filled that cloud up until there was no room left for the cloud. It's not a monster. It's what's left when the water won't stop.

kraken_drizzle.speaker: patch
kraken_drizzle.text: I thought it was just the bad guy. It's easier when it's just the bad guy.
